definition: Each object either has an incoming cause or causes some numerically distinct other object; the disjunction is inclusive. This is the strict premise used by the formal argument, not a defeasible default or a modal universal.
note: Primary P3p126–127 is the strict displayed premise. Rutten p131 limits it to actual reality and also calls a default/exception-permitting version sufficient. This reading does not promote that default to the strict universal: whether a suitably restricted default supports the proof remains open.
